question: Have anyone tried training with 4-bit quantization? Did you observe some performance difference with higher precision?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Directly answers affirmatively by naming QLoRA and describing its approach: gradients are backpropagated through a frozen 4-bit quantized pretrained model into LoRA adapters.
examples: QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized LLM into Low Rank Adapters
The pretrained model is kept frozen at 4-bit while LoRA adapters are trained

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: States the central empirical finding: 4-bit QLoRA with the NF4 data type matches both 16-bit full fine-tuning and 16-bit LoRA performance on academic benchmarks, with no observed degradation.
examples: 4-bit NF4 QLoRA matches 16-bit full finetuning and 16-bit LoRA performance
We did not observe performance degradation compared to full finetuning at 16-bit

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Explains that for a fixed compute/memory budget, results (MMLU, Elo) indicate it is beneficial to increase the number of base-model parameters while decreasing their precision.
examples: MMLU and Elo results suggest increasing parameters while decreasing precision is beneficial
Larger 4-bit models outperform smaller 16-bit models under a fixed budget

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Cites at least one concrete performance figure, e.g., Guanaco 65B reaching 99.3% of ChatGPT on the Vicuna benchmark, 30% expected win probability vs GPT-4, or Guanaco 33B at 4-bit (21GB) beating Vicuna 13B (26GB).
examples: Guanaco 65B achieves 99.3% of ChatGPT performance on the Vicuna benchmark
Guanaco 33B at 4-bit (21GB) outperforms Vicuna 13B (26GB) by three percentage points

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Quantifies the efficiency motivation: 4-bit quantization enables fine-tuning a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU in 24 hours, or deployment footprints like 7B at 5GB on phones.
examples: QLoRA reduces memory enough to fine-tune a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU
Guanaco 7B fits on modern phones with a 5GB footprint

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Describes at least one QLoRA-specific technique: NF4 (information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights, more effective than FP4), double quantization of quantization constants, or paged optimizers.
examples: NF4 is a new data type that is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed weights and beats FP4
Paged optimizers manage memory spikes during training

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Notes the breadth of evaluation: over 1,000 models fine-tuned across 8 instruction datasets, model types (LLaMA, T5), and scales up to 65B.
examples: QLoRA was used to finetune over 1,000 models across 8 instruction datasets
Experiments covered LLaMA and T5 models up to 65B parameters

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Concludes that 4-bit training is effective and efficient with little to no observed loss, while acknowledging the exact performance–precision trade-off for QLoRA tuning remains open and left to future work.
examples: The authors leave the precise performance-precision trade-off to future work
Overall, 4-bit quantization enables efficient training without meaningful performance deterioration in the studied setups
